## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T652 (three fascicles) is the Northern Song retranslation by [紹德](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%B4%B9%E5%BE%B7) (Shàodé) and his team at the Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* of the same Indic *sūtra* underlying [T650](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0288) (Kumārajīva) and [T651](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0289) (Jñānagupta). The title — emphasizing the *suízhuǎn* "subsequent turning" of the dharma-wheel — reflects the Song-period preference for narratively-framed *prajñāpāramitā* expositions.

**Abstract**

[紹德](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%B4%B9%E5%BE%B7) (Shàodé) was a Chinese-trained monk at the imperial *Yìjīng yuàn* established by [宋太宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E5%A4%AA%E5%AE%97) Sòng Tàizōng in 982; he served as a translation assistant and later as a lead translator alongside Indian masters such as [Shīhù / Dānapāla](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7). Date bracket follows the active period of the *Yìjīng yuàn*'s first generation (980–1015). The translation reflects a substantially expanded Indic recension relative to Kumārajīva's T650, with additional bodhisattva-doctrine passages that show the influence of late-Indian Mahāyāna *paripṛcchā* literature. Together with T650 and T651, T652 forms the three Chinese versions of the *Sarvadharmapravṛttinirdeśa* tradition.
